Harbor Town v. Ferry Company

The town sued the ferry company over the reconstructed tide entries in its ledger, and the court has heard the first of its arguments, which turn on whether the half-fathom rounding in the ferry's logbooks

The town sued the ferry company over the reconstructed tide entries in its ledger. The harbor master had copied two lost February readings from the ferry's logbooks, which round every depth to the nearest half fathom, and marked both with a circle in the margin. The company argued that the circles were enough notice; the town argued that a ledger used to set mooring fees must say how precise each entry is. The court held a first hearing in the spring and asked both sides for the logbooks of the three winters before.

Questions people ask

Why were two entries lost?

The old ledger was left beside a window through the winter storms, and its pages swelled and stuck together along their lower edges. A bookbinder from the next valley eased them apart over three afternoons, and only the two February entries could not be read again.

Is the ledger on view?

On weekday mornings.
